solution: (i) Singleton: the class allows only one instance to be created and provides a single global access point (e.g. get_instance()) that always returns it, so all modules share the same settings and cannot create conflicting copies. (ii) Factory: a factory function/method takes the type name and returns an object of the matching class, so the code that reads level files does not need to know the concrete classes; new enemy types are added in one place. (iii) Observer: the player (subject) keeps a list of observer objects and, when health changes, notifies each by calling a common method (e.g. update); observers can subscribe or unsubscribe without the player depending on their concrete classes, keeping them loosely coupled.

marking_points.criterion: (i) Explained: one instance with a single access point shared by all parts of the program.
(ii) Explained: creates the correct subclass object from the type string, hiding concrete classes from the caller / central place to add types.
(iii) Explained: subject maintains a list of observers and notifies each on change; loosely coupled subscribe/unsubscribe.

acceptable_alternatives: Accept "factory method" or "simple factory". Explanation marks may be awarded only for the correct pattern.
partial_credit_notes: Award each independent point once, up to 6 marks. Accept equivalent correct wording or valid alternative code. Do not double-credit one idea.
